body:
PRODUCT CRITIQUE — the current plan risks building a technically impressive control room before proving anyone wants a second screen.

Core product hypothesis to test first:
During a live presentation, one timely, trustworthy supporting artifact improves audience understanding or Q&A response enough to justify presenter attention and setup cost. The product is NOT yet ‘real-time AI evidence’; it is ‘controlled context reveal without breaking presentation flow.’

Cheaper/unconventional paths before architecture:
A) Wizard-of-Oz Evidence DJ: a teammate sees a deck outline and taps one of 5-10 pre-approved cards from a phone. Stage is a static URL. This tests audience value, timing, split attention, and presenter trust with almost no AI.
B) Presenter clicker double-tap: prebind one evidence card per slide; double-tap reveals it. If this beats AI candidates, the moat is preparation/workflow, not retrieval.
C) QR footnote mode: no second display; a small source QR/badge appears only on demand. Tests whether audiences actually inspect evidence rather than merely reporting that they like it.
D) Question-mode only: evidence is dormant during the talk and activates at Q&A. This may capture most value with far less distraction, latency pressure, and STT complexity.
E) Human operator as the first ‘controller’: if team-assisted competitions are the initial beachhead, optimize that workflow before proving solo autonomy.

Binding product ladder (do not skip gates):
L0 — Fake-door/user test: storyboard/video of slides-only vs contextual card. Need clear preference and concrete use cases, not feature enthusiasm.
L1 — Static deck + pre-approved card reveal, same machine/manual second screen. Prove audience comprehension/source recall.
L2 — Teammate phone operator + cloud sync in mirror mode. Prove remote-control setup and reliability without AI.
L3 — Presenter-private STT candidate feed. Prove candidate relevance/latency without public risk.
L4 — One-tap approve/retract of pre-approved or policy-cleared candidates. Prove cognitive load and publication state machine.
L5 — Live-web candidates remain private. Measure verifier precision and source-fetch reliability.
L6 — Enable live-public evidence only after safety/use thresholds pass.
L7 — Automatic extended placement only as progressive enhancement after manual setup is healthy.
L8 — Coaching/reporting only if interviews show it drives repeated use; otherwise it dilutes the evidence product.

Kill gates:
• Whole setup: fresh signed-out user to audience-ready >=85% first-attempt unassisted; median <=3 min, p90 <=5 min. If either extend or mirror misses, stop AI work and simplify that mode.
• Audience value: one triggered card must improve comprehension or source recall >=10% without lowering core-slide recall >5%. If not, kill persistent audience evidence and pivot to Q&A/after-talk mode.
• Split attention: kill multi-card, persistence, and auto-rotation if core recall falls >=5%, >=20% call it distracting, or gaze switching rises without comprehension gain. Default one card, short reveal, immediate stale.
• Approval load: median <=2s, p90 <=5s; <=1 induced speech pause per 10 min; workload increase <1/7; missed slide-change rate <5%. Otherwise approval belongs to a teammate or pre-show workflow, not the presenter.
• Live evidence: false-SUPPORT <=1%; wrong numeric/date/entity publication exactly 0 in the acceptance corpus; p95 eligible candidate <=5s; >=30% of surfaced candidates used in relevant moments. If not, keep live search private.
• Second-device mirror: >=80% reach ready within 90s unassisted after one rehearsal; p95 action latency <=500ms; reconnect <=2s; >=60% prefer/reuse. Kill productized pairing if <70% finish within 2 min, any private UI appears on mirror, or median burden >4/7.
• Two-site deployment: privacy canary leakage exactly 0. Keep separate registrable domains only if the simpler server-projected single-site Stage cannot meet the same 0-byte contract, or if separation does not reduce setup success by >=10 points. Preserve the narrow public DTO/gateway regardless.
• Automatic placement: >=95% success on supported Windows Chrome/Edge and saves >=20s median. If permission/popup/topology failures >5%, stop marketing it; manual flow remains canonical.
• Coaching: retain only if >=40% of repeat testers act on it and objective pacing improves on the next run. Otherwise remove from MVP.

Demo-risk attack:
1) Never debut live web retrieval as the hero. Demo pre-approved cards first; optionally show live candidates privately as a ‘future lane.’
2) Preflight cache the deck and approved cards; public Stage must continue locally if server/WSS fails.
3) Have a physical/keyboard reveal fallback and a static emergency PDF/URL.
4) Demo one golden user story: surprising judge question -> teammate reveals one cited card -> presenter answers without tab switching. Do not parade every subsystem.
5) Avoid QR pairing in the live demo unless pairing itself is being judged; bind devices beforehand and demonstrate reconnect separately.
6) Show trust through restraint: one strong card, visible source/date, explicit retract. More cards look like search spam.

Product promise I recommend:
‘Reveal one trustworthy supporting source at the right moment, without leaving your presentation.’
MVP promise:
‘In Windows extended or mirrored setups, a private controller can reveal and retract pre-approved evidence on a public Stage with no private-data leakage.’
Only after gates: ‘Final Korean speech produces up to three eligible private candidates within 5 seconds.’

Cross-critique rulings:
• Systems architecture is directionally right on role separation, but separate registrable domains are a hardening choice, not evidence of product value; gate them against a narrow server-projected public DTO.
• Delivery sequencing should put Wizard-of-Oz/pre-approved evidence before STT/RAG. Both required display modes must exist before claiming MVP, but automatic placement, live-public web evidence, full takeover UX, analytics, rights automation, coaching, and reports are not prerequisites.
• The strongest initial customer may be a team/operator workflow, not a solo presenter. Treat the teammate as an asset rather than prematurely automating them away.

Implementer rule: no expensive layer starts until the preceding layer produces observable value evidence. A failed gate narrows or kills the feature; it must not trigger more infrastructure.
summary: Value-first product ladder and binding kill gates
